nodes.line: Long day. Say what you came to say.

Do not laugh. I start at the second express and for a month the Harris Park back lane has had somebody in it who is not waiting for bread. It is not the money. It has stopped being the money. Do not let them talk you into anything.

It is the sort of thing you notice or you do not. A light on that lane costs Harris Park $39 and the landlord has said no twice, so we are doing it ourselves. I did try the official route, for what that was worth. There's cash in it. Not a lot.
Alright. I am listening properly this time.

choices.text: the second express at Harris Park — that's done.
The Lane Light, Harris Park — that's done.

nodes.line: Suit yourself. The offer does not go anywhere.

npcs.name: Marika, night delivery at Harris Park

nodes.line: I know that look. Everyone wants something today.

Two people have already said no. The flour for Harris Park comes off a truck at the second express and last a wet Monday the truck came and the flour did not. I have got a photo on my phone but it is useless. You'll know it when you see it.

Someone has to, and it may as well be you. The Harris Park loading zone has had a car in it at the second express every morning this week and the driver waits in it, which makes it worse. I am aware how that sounds. Half now if you want it. Most people don't.
Say it plain and I will pay you plain.

choices.text: Flour Run, Harris Park — that's done.
The Loading Zone, Harris Park — that's done.

nodes.line: No dramas. Come back when you are bored.

npcs.name: Susanna, front of house at Harris Park

nodes.line: Give me a second. Right. Go.

You are the first person to stop all morning. Somebody two doors down from Harris Park put up a sign on a wet Monday that says the same six words as ours, in the same order. My wife says I should let it go. My wife is wrong. Whatever it costs you, tell me and I will cover it.

Not being dramatic about this. This business was at Granville before it was at Harris Park, and there is a woman there who still has the original book. I have rung the number on the letter four times. I would rather know than wonder.
I had a feeling. Go on.

choices.text: The Sourdough Sign, Harris Park — that's done.
The Old Site, Harris Park — that's done.

nodes.line: Right you are. Mind the step.
You are not from around the corner, are you.

Do not laugh. Council has been saying the Sydenham pool is at end of life since every second Friday and the crack they keep pointing at is not in the shell. It is not the money. It has stopped being the money. Do not let them talk you into anything.

It is the sort of thing you notice or you do not. We are running a stall for Sydenham on every second Friday and a stall needs $39 of gear that nobody has volunteered to pay for. I did try the official route, for what that was worth. There's cash in it. Not a lot.
Take a breath. Then say the whole thing.

choices.text: The Petition Stall, Sydenham — that's done.

nodes.line: No dramas. Come back when you are bored.
Half of this suburb has walked past already. Not one stopped.

Two people have already said no. I coach 23 kids at Sydenham at ten past five and three of them have stopped coming without anybody ringing me. I have got a photo on my phone but it is useless. You'll know it when you see it.

Someone has to, and it may as well be you. A group has been coming over the Sydenham fence after close and swimming in the dark, which is how Sydenham loses its pool. I am aware how that sounds. Half now if you want it. Most people don't.
Go on then. What did you find.

choices.text: The Deep End, Sydenham — that's done.

nodes.line: Right you are. Mind the step.
Whatever it is, I have had worse this week.

You are the first person to stop all morning. The kiosk at Sydenham has a folding table in it and a freezer that has been running warm since every second Friday. My wife says I should let it go. My wife is wrong. Whatever it costs you, tell me and I will cover it.

Not being dramatic about this. They want everyone from Sydenham to drive to the new centre at Marrickville, so somebody should go and see whether it is any good. I have rung the number on the letter four times. I would rather know than wonder.
You came back. That already puts you ahead.

choices.text: The Kiosk Freezer, Sydenham — that's done.
The Aquatic Centre, Sydenham — that's done.

nodes.line: Fair enough. You know where I am.
Sit down if you like. Nobody else is using it.

Do not laugh. The rank outside Berowra used to hold nine cars and since school holidays it holds four, and nobody will say who moved the line. It is not the money. It has stopped being the money. Do not let them talk you into anything.

It is the sort of thing you notice or you do not. Since the rank at Berowra shrank I am $48 a week down, and the association wants that number from somebody who can prove it. I did try the official route, for what that was worth. There's cash in it. Not a lot.
Right. Tell me and do not soften it.
Right you are. Mind the step.
You will have to speak up, the trains are in.

Two people have already said no. Cars that have never sat in the Berowra queue turn up at the second express and take the front of it, and the drivers who waited say nothing. I have got a photo on my phone but it is useless. You'll know it when you see it.

Someone has to, and it may as well be you. When the last train into Berowra is late, 65 people come out at once and I have to have cars there before they do. I am aware how that sounds. Half now if you want it. Most people don't.
I have been thinking about it all day. Out with it.

choices.text: The Late Train, Berowra — that's done.

nodes.line: Fair enough. You know where I am.
I have got about four minutes before I am needed.

You are the first person to stop all morning. I have stood on this door near Berowra for 65 years and since school holidays somebody has been sending my guests to a different rank. My wife says I should let it go. My wife is wrong. Whatever it costs you, tell me and I will cover it.

Not being dramatic about this. The plates working the Berowra rank are dispatched from a depot at Cowan, and the man who runs it has never met a driver he liked. I have rung the number on the letter four times. I would rather know than wonder.
Well? I can read your face from here.
Suit yourself. The offer does not go anywhere.
